meta.title: Horizon: Minecraft Rust Edition, Java 26.3 rewritten in Rust
meta.description: Minecraft: Java Edition 26.3 rewritten in Rust. Free, open source and tested against vanilla. Get the Horizon launcher for Windows, macOS and Linux.

footer.disclaimer: Not an official Minecraft product. Not approved by or associated with Mojang or Microsoft.
footer.who: Horizon is made by Ludovic Marie; reach him through <lu4ovic>lu4ovic.com</lu4ovic>. This site is developed by Anthony S of <dezerx>DezerX</dezerx>, who is responsible for it. Horizon contains no Minecraft code, assets or data, and this site offers no game files: you need your own legally obtained copy of Minecraft: Java Edition. Minecraft is a trademark of Mojang Synergies AB. Horizon's cosmetics are sold by Ludovic Marie through Paddle.com, the merchant of record.
footer.licences: Horizon's original work is under the <mit>MIT licence</mit>. The fonts are Geist, Geist Mono and Bricolage Grotesque, under the <ofl>SIL Open Font License</ofl>. Every asset on this site is listed in LEGAL.md.
footer.privacy: This site sets no cookies, has no analytics or trackers and loads nothing from third parties except GitHub. When you open a release, the server keeps a one-way hash of your IP address so that release counts each visitor once; the address itself is never stored. To show the latest releases, patch notes, links and contributors, your browser asks api.github.com and raw.githubusercontent.com for them, and avatars.githubusercontent.com for the contributors' pictures; <github>GitHub's privacy statement</github> covers those requests. The launcher sends nothing unless you allow it: <telemetry>what it can send, and how to delete it</telemetry>.
footer.madeInRust: Made in the open, in Rust.

about.title: Same inputs, identical outputs.
about.lead: Horizon, sometimes called Minecraft Rust Edition, rebuilds Minecraft: Java Edition 26.3 in Rust, one subsystem at a time, and holds every piece to the same inputs as the vanilla game until the outputs are identical.
about.imageAlt: A Minecraft windmill above a field of lavender

copy.title: Your own copy
copy.body: Install Java Edition with the official launcher and play 26.3 once. Horizon builds its resources from those files on your machine, and never downloads or shares game files.

native.title: Native on three platforms
native.body: Linux, macOS on Apple Silicon or Intel, and Windows on x64 or ARM. Worlds come from a Rust port of the vanilla generators, drawn with vanilla's block models, lighting, sky and fog.

open.title: Open source

parity.title: Where the project started.
parity.lead: Below is the project's first audit of each subsystem: what its harnesses compared then, and how much of it they covered. It is not a parity claim: players still find differences, and parity work on 26.3 continues, redstone first.
parity.audited: Audited <date/><dot/>players still find differences: <link>the open reports</link>

scale.1: its harnesses cover it and pass

loop.name: Window, input and game loop
loop.detail: The game loop, options, camera, auto-jump, toggle sprint/sneak, local input and the frame limiter match vanilla.

assets.name: Assets and resources
assets.detail: Item models match vanilla over 196,290 stacks and the client draws every item through them; the resource pack screen matches vanilla's drawing over 3,000 sessions of clicks, scrolling and searching, its incompatibility confirmation included.

network.name: Network protocol and multiplayer
network.detail: Joins vanilla servers; the dedicated server (--dedicated) matches vanilla's files, status ping, login, configuration, play, chunks, chat, recipes, advancements and command tree, a client built from vanilla's packet code joins it, Horizon joins a vanilla server, and LAN discovery matches over 462 cases (offline mode only).

chunks.name: Chunk storage and palettes
chunks.detail: Client and saves share paletted containers, identical to vanilla over 266 scenarios.

meshing.name: Section meshing
meshing.detail: 112 scenes and over a million quads identical to vanilla.

rendering.name: Rendering
rendering.detail: Entity models, block entity renderers (407 cases, End portals, gateways and the loom's banner preview included) and their animations (296 cases, End gateway beams included), the HUD overlays (2,200 states), the recipe book (600 states), the player list, subtitles and the world border match vanilla.

lighting.name: Lighting
lighting.detail: Saved and relit light matches vanilla, slabs and stairs included.

worldgen.name: World generation
worldgen.detail: 2,352 whole chunks over 225 structure sites, in all three dimensions, identical to vanilla.

saves.name: Region files and saves
saves.detail: Saves round-trip with vanilla, and worlds from 1.8 to 26.2 upgrade as vanilla's DataFixers do, superflat worlds included; old options.txt and hotbar.nbt files are upgraded too.

entities.name: Entities and physics
entities.detail: Attributes, dimensions, death loot, spawn rules, natural spawning (15,500 cases), raids and patrols (1,900 cases), spawned mobs' gear, enchantments and state (finalizeSpawn, 24,000 cases) and mob AI (92 scenarios: villager breeding and gossip, the warden, ghastlings and copper golems included) match vanilla.

inventory.name: Interaction and inventory
inventory.detail: Menu clicks match over 8,000 click sequences, the loom and the crafter included; recipe book placement (6,000 cases), its buttons (1,200), the saved book (1,500) and the loom and crafter screens (1,600) match vanilla.

menus.name: Menus, HUD and chat
menus.detail: Every command runs as vanilla (758 commands over 39,685 parsed inputs), scoreboards and teams match (81,000 operations), the player list matches over 872,000 draw calls with heads drawn from players' skins (authlib's textures, SkinManager's lookup, legacy skin conversion), and the chat matches focused and scrolled; the resource pack screen (selection over 4,000 cases, drawing and its incompatibility confirmation over 3,000 sessions) and the chat input with its command suggestions, usage lines, Tab completion and history (3,000 sessions on vanilla's client command tree) match vanilla.

audio.name: Audio
audio.detail: The sound engine, sound events, music, situational music, ambience and subtitles match vanilla.

blocks.name: Block behaviours and ticking
blocks.detail: Block updates, random ticks, redstone, dispensers (6,000 cases), crafters (4,000 crafts), block entity removal (containers spill, 4,000 cases), copper golem chest sorting and the sculk family (435 scenarios: shrieker warnings and warden summoning included) match vanilla.

meta.title: Horizon vs Minecraft Java benchmarks: FPS, memory, loading
meta.description: Horizon against Minecraft: Java Edition 26.3 on a 2016 ThinkPad, a Mac mini and a gaming desktop: frame rates, hitches, loading and memory, measured alike.

benchmarks.lead: The same three computers ran both games through the same world, on the same flight path, with the same settings. Here is what you would notice, in plain words, including where Java Edition still wins.

summary.noHitches: No hitches at all in Horizon; {java} a minute in Java Edition.
summary.fewer: About {pct}% fewer hitches, and {h} FPS on average against {v}.
summary.leadMore: Horizon averages {pct}% more FPS at render distance 12
summary.leadSame: Both games average about the same at render distance 12

metrics.low1: Frame rate in the worst moments

losses.title: Where Java Edition is still faster
losses.intro: Every case in these runs where the original game did better. Steadier frames at long render distances is on the <link>roadmap</link> as work being done now.

yours.title: What about your computer?
yours.lead: Pick your graphics card and processor. The estimate starts from the measured computer closest to yours and scales it by the chips' specifications, so it is a range, not a promise.

method.title: How it was measured
method.p1: Each game starts from a fresh world (seed 1234, creative), waits until every chunk around the spawn is loaded and drawn, then visits a village, a forest, an ocean and a mountain. At each it waits for the terrain, holds for 2 seconds and flies a straight 192-block path in 12 seconds, recording every frame.
method.p2: VSync off, no frame cap, a 1280x720 window, simulation distance 12, everything else at vanilla's defaults. Java Edition 26.3 runs as players get it, with the official launcher's Java options. Each figure is the median over the runs{measured}.
method.p3: The full method and its caveats are in <link>docs/benchmark.md</link>.

own.title: Benchmark your own computer
own.lead: Run this in a terminal. It flies the same path and writes a report to the benchmarks folder of the game folder. Share it on Discord and your machine helps make these numbers better.

explorer.pickLead: Three of the project's own machines, from a 2016 laptop to a gaming desktop.

verdict.never: Horizon never dipped below 60 FPS on the {machine}; Java Edition did {java} times a minute.
verdict.fewer: On the {machine}, Horizon hitched {h} times a minute against Java Edition's {v}.
verdict.javaSmoother: On the {machine}, Java Edition ran smoother here: {v} hitches a minute against Horizon's {h}.
verdict.same: On the {machine}, both games stayed about as smooth.
verdict.javaFaster: Java Edition got into the world faster.

hitches.title: Hitches in a minute of play
hitches.body: A hitch is a frame slower than one refresh of a 60 Hz screen, so you see the same picture twice. Red marks are the long ones, under 30 FPS, that you feel as a stutter.
hitches.stutters: Long stutters a minute: Horizon {h}, Java Edition {v}.

fps.title: Frames per second
fps.capped: Horizon is held at {n} here by the Mac's display, so its average can't go higher. Look at the worst moments.

memory.title: Memory while playing
memory.needs: Java Edition needs {times} more, which matters on a computer with 8 GB.

feel.title: Feel the difference
feel.lead: Both views pan at the same speed, but each one only moves when its game finishes a frame, using the frame times measured on the {machine} at render distance {rd}. Every freeze and jump you see is a hitch.
feel.note: A replay of the measured distribution of frame times, not a recording. Your screen shows at most its own refresh rate, so in real time every frame faster than that looks the same. {n}x slower plays the same frames at a quarter of the speed, so each one stays up long enough to see.

estimator.headlineExact: Measured on this exact pair: {h} FPS in Horizon's worst moments, against {v} in Java Edition.
estimator.headline: Expect roughly {h} FPS in Horizon's worst moments, against {v} in Java Edition.
estimator.line: {range} FPS on average · in the world in {low} to {high} s
estimator.measured: These are the figures measured on {machine}.
estimator.scaled: Scaled from {machine}, the measured computer closest to yours, by the two chips' published specifications.
estimator.caveat: Drivers, cooling and the operating system can matter as much as the chip, so treat it as a rough idea and run the benchmark below for your real figure.

meta.title: 3D artists · Horizon
meta.description: Horizon welcomes 3D artists to make cosmetics for its players: hats, back items, shoulder pets, trails and emotes in a blocky style. Say hello on Discord.

artists.lead: Horizon welcomes 3D artists to make cosmetics for Horizon players: things players wear and carry that other Horizon players see in every world and on every server. If you like making small, blocky models, we'd like to hear from you.

make.title: What we'd make together
items: Back items, such as backpacks or rigid wings.
Small pets that ride on a player's shoulder, or companions that float beside them.
Auras and trails made of a few particles.
Emotes: short animations for the player's own model.
make.note: Cosmetics only change how a player looks, never how the game plays.

fits.title: What fits
items: Low-poly models in Minecraft's blocky style, built from a few dozen cubes, with small pixel textures (16 to 64 pixels).
Your own designs. No copies of Minecraft's mobs and items, or of anyone else's work.
Art for every age, that still reads at a distance.
No capes, or anything that hangs from the shoulders like one.
Blockbench is welcome. Animation is a plus, not a requirement.

contact.title: Get in touch
contact.body: Join Horizon's Discord and say you're a 3D artist, with a few pieces you've made: links or pictures are fine. If you'd rather write privately, write through <link>lu4ovic.com</link>.
